sentences.text: The charts present the findings of a survey on consumers’ acceptance of elderly-care robots and their primary concerns.
sentences.read: The charts present the findings of a survey on consumers' acceptance of elderly-care robots and their primary concerns.

sentences.text: As the pie chart shows, 39.3% of the respondents fully accept these robots and another 32.8% accept them partially, while the remaining 27.9% reject them altogether.
sentences.read: As the pie chart shows, thirty-nine point three percent of the respondents fully accept these robots and another thirty-two point eight percent accept them partially, while the remaining twenty-seven point nine percent reject them altogether.

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the bar chart reveals that safety tops consumers’ concerns at 46.3%, far ahead of price (24.9%) and convenience (10.7%).
sentences.read: Meanwhile, the bar chart reveals that safety tops consumers' concerns at forty-six point three percent, far ahead of price, twenty-four point nine percent, and convenience, ten point seven percent.

sentences.text: Several factors may account for these figures.

sentences.text: On the one hand, as the population ages rapidly and professional caregivers are in short supply, more and more families regard robots as a practical way to care for elderly relatives, which explains why over 70% of consumers are open to them.

sentences.text: On the other hand, elderly people are physically fragile, so even a minor malfunction could cause serious harm.

sentences.text: Hence, safety ranks first, and some consumers reject the robots altogether.

sentences.text: In my view, elderly-care robots have a promising future, but their popularity depends on public trust.

sentences.text: Manufacturers should give top priority to safety and reliability, while the government ought to set strict standards and offer subsidies to make these products affordable.
